signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-17 ppt-web-core websocket auth transport) — adopted by routine
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:94-101 — buildWebSocketUrl(base, token) appends the full JWT access token to the handshake URL as a query parameter: `url.searchParams.set('token', token)`. openConnection() (:369) then opens `new WebSocket(buildWebSocketUrl(this.url, token), ['ppt.v1'])`, so the raw bearer JWT rides in the WS connect URL on every (re)connect.

Full request URLs including query strings are routinely captured in reverse-proxy / load-balancer / CDN access logs, APM traces, browser history, and devtools network panel. A leaked access JWT is a bearer credential; anyone who reads it from a log can replay it until it expires. wss:// protects on the wire but not at rest.

Suggested hardening: short-lived, single-use WS 'ticket' endpoint (POST /ws/ticket → opaque nonce valid ~30s / one connection) so the WS URL carries `?ticket=<nonce>` instead of the JWT. Cheaper mitigation: backend-side strip/redact WS handshake query strings from all access logs. Note: same `?token=` pattern likely exists in reality-web and mobile WS clients — sweep together.
